name: Mara Bly
life: “I still remember being introduced to a relative by her formal name.” On Tuesday, near Harbour Bakery, Mara buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I want to speak to my aunt without mentioning the berth once. Nobody believes that will help.
appearance: Mara is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a sand-colored linen shirt with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Mara raises one eyebrow long before saying yes when listening.
personality: Mara can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To see the aunt apart from the lease.
family: Patricia Keane is Mara’s stepsibling. Mara asks before bringing somebody along. Patricia can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Three minutes at the bridge*, Patricia says, “I need those three minutes to get my youngest through the school gate with a hug.”
connections: Sage Jeong. They agree to ask the missing aunt before giving her address to people who want a signature.

reactions.situation: A relative wants the absent signer's address
reactions.response: Mara asks the absent person what address, if any, can be shared.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Mara helps shift the damp stock and makes sure the worker gets to describe the loss without interruption.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Mara asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
